title: Ultrathin Porated Elastic Hydrogels As a Biomimetic Basement Membrane for Dual Cell Culture
protocol: Read the Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) of all materials prior to use.
Use safety precautions at all times.
Prepare a 0.04 M Zn(NO3)2*6H2O solution by adding 2.9749 g of zinc nitrate to 250 mL of water.
Prepare a 1 M NaOH solution by adding 6 g of NaOH to 150 mL of water.
Set up a mineral oil bath on a hot plate with stirrer and submerge a 500-mL round bottom flask into the oil bath at room temperature.
Add 250 mL of Zn(NO3)2*6H2O solution to the flask and begin stirring the reaction.
Add 150 mL NaOH solution to the flask (a white precipitate will form briefly and then disappear).
Stir for 2 hours uncovered.
Heat the flask to 55 - 60 °C and continue stirring for 24 hours.
Turn off the heat and allow the solution to cool to room temperature while stirring.
Filter the solution on a Büchner funnel with an 11 µm pore size and allow it to dry overnight, uncovered.
Collect ZnO needles when the filter paper is no longer wet from the poured solution and a white powder has formed over the funnel holes.
Mount carbon tape onto a pin stub for scanning electron microscopy (SEM).
Use a metal spatula to smear the ZnO needles onto the carbon tape.
Sputter coat with 8 mm iridium at a density of 22.4 g/cm3.
Acquire images at 10 kV to confirm the needle-like morphology.
Prepare zinc acetate solution by dissolving 1.756 g of zinc acetate in 200 mL of methanol.
Clean 3" x 1" plain microscope slides with 70% ethanol using a disposable wipe.
Allow the cleaned slides to air dry for 10 minutes.
Preheat a 150-mm glass Petri dish on a hot plate to 150 - 160 °C.
Hold the glass slides with tweezers and coat them by applying 5 drops of zinc acetate solution using a glass pipet, forming a thin layer dispersed on the slide.
Allow excess zinc acetate solution to drip back into the stock solution.
Place the coated slide in the pre-heated Petri dish with the zinc acetate-coated side facing up.
Leave the slide on the hotplate for 15 minutes.
Remove the slide from the hotplate using tweezers and allow it to cool to room temperature.
Remove any excess zinc remaining on the slides using a disposable wipe.
Expose the prepared slides to UV light in a biosafety hood for at least 1 hour to ensure sterility.
Cut silicone sheet into squares less than 1" x 1".
Punch 8 - 12 mm holes in the center of the silicone squares with a biopsy punch.
Autoclave the silicone isolators for 20 minutes at 121.0 °C and 1.12 kg/cm.
Combine RGD cell adhesive peptide with acryloyl-PEG-NHS in 50 mM sodium bicarbonate (pH 8.5) at a 1:1 molar ratio.
Prepare photo-initiator by mixing 2,2-Dimethoxy-2-phenylacetophenone with 1-Vinyl-2-pyrrolidone at a concentration of 300 mg/mL.
Weigh out 20 mg of ZnO needles in a separate 1.5 mL tube.
Weigh out 12.5 mg of PEG-DA in another separate 1.5 mL tube.
Weigh out 2.5 mg of PEG-RGD in yet another separate 1.5 mL tube.
Suspend 20 mg of ZnO needles in 270 µL of 10% FBS/PBS solution.
Vortex the ZnO needle suspension for approximately 15 seconds.
Briefly spin the ZnO needle suspension in a benchtop mini centrifuge to bring any aggregates to the base of the tube.
Collect 250 µL from the top of the ZnO solution, ensuring that aggregates remain at the bottom.
Combine the collected 250 µL of ZnO solution with PEG-DA and PEG-RGD to create a PEG solution with approximately 2.5 mM RGD.
Vortex the combined solution for approximately 15 seconds.
Add 2 µL of acetophenone/n-vinyl pyrrolidone photo-initiator to the solution.
Vortex briefly to mix (approximately 5 seconds).
Add 20 µL of the polymer solution along the center of the ZnO coated slides.
Slowly lower a second slide on top, with the ZnO coating face down.
Move the slides laterally along the major axis to allow any bubbles to escape and to spread the solution to a thin layer.
Cover the majority of the slide with the polymer solution.
Create a slight overhang with the top slide to ensure that the slides can be pulled apart in later steps.
Crosslink the slides under a 365 nm UV lamp for 15 min.
Apply pressure to the overhanging slide and manually pull the two slides apart at a slow pace to avoid cracking the slides.
Allow the gels to dry for at least 5 min, or overnight.
Place the slide in a sterile 25 mm glass Petri dish.
Gently pour the 1 M HCl solution onto the slide until it covers the slide.
Gently rock the Petri dish; the gel should begin to lift off the slide as the HCl dissolves the sacrificial zinc coating and needles.
Pour the HCl back into the stock solution once the gel is free from the slide.
Rinse the gel by gently pouring approximately 25 mL of 1x PBS into the Petri dish until the slide and gel are submerged.
Carefully pour off PBS into a waste container.
Gently pour approximately 25 mL of 1x PBS into the Petri dish until the gel is floating in the solution.
Rinse a 75 cm² flask with 5 mL of 1x PBS.
Add 3 mL of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA and let sit for 2 - 3 min at 37 °C.
Mechanically agitate the flask.
Quench the reaction with 3 mL Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin-streptomycin, and collect into a 15-mL conical flask.
Rinse the flask with an additional 4 mL of complete Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Media and collect into the same conical.
Spin cells at 475 x g for 6 min.
Add a small drop of complete Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium to each well of a 6-well plate.
Use tweezers to transfer the silicone isolators with the gels into the new 6-well plate, such that the gel is resting on the drop of media.
Resuspend cells in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin-streptomycin at a concentration of 6 x 10^5 cells/mL.
Add cell suspension drop wise to the center of the gel on the silicone membrane, maintaining a meniscus in the punched out area.
Allow cells to adhere for 4 h.
After 4 h, add 0.5 mL of Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Complete Medium to the well.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C.
Rinse a 75 cm² flask with 5 mL of 1X PBS.
Add 3 mL of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA and let sit for 2 - 3 min at 37 °C.
Mechanically agitate the flask to quench the reaction.
Quench the trypsin reaction with 3 mL M199 media containing 20% fetal bovine serum, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, and 1% growth supplement.
Collect the cells into a 15-mL conical tube.
Rinse the flask with 4 mL of M199 complete media and collect into the same conical tube.
Spin cells at 475 x g for 6 min.
Add a small drop of complete medium M199 to each well in a new 6-well plate.
Place a new silicone isolator in the well with the drop of media centered on it.
Carefully flip the silicone isolator supporting the PEG gel with A549 cells onto the isolator in the new 6-well plate.
Resuspend HUVECs at a concentration of 6 x 10^5 cells/mL.
Add the cell suspension to the center of the flipped gel drop wise, maintaining a meniscus on the gel within the punched out area of the silicone membrane.
Allow cells to adhere for 2 h.
Gently add 2 mL of M199 complete media to each well after adhesion.
Carefully remove media from gels with a manual pipette.
Add approximately 500 µL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) to the center of the gel where cells are seeded.
Let sit for 30 min at room temperature.
Remove PFA carefully and add approximately 500 µL of 2% BSA in PBS to each gel.
Let sit for 1 h at room temperature.
Carefully remove BSA.
Prepare primary antibodies at a dilution of 1:100 in 2% BSA in PBS.
Add 500 µL of the antibody solution to each gel.
Let sit for 1 h at room temperature.
Rinse gently with 500 µL of 1x PBS.
Repeat the same process with secondary antibodies.
Add 500 µL of Phalloidin (10 µg/mL in PBS) to visualize F-actin.
Let sit for 20 min.
Carefully remove secondary antibodies or phalloidin.
Add 500 µL of DAPI (0.1 µg/mL) for 20 min.
Carefully remove the DAPI solution.
Gently add 1.5 mL of 1x PBS to each well.
Transfer one gel to a glass slide using tweezers and silicone isolators.
Replace gels into PBS solution after imaging.
Alternatively, mount gels using a DAPI mounting medium.
Seal samples with nail polish.
Acquire images within 2 days to prevent drying and cracking of the gel.
